node_definition.done_when:
Read section 12 of scoring-should-stop-a-promotion first. Reproduce first. At your base, recover() in reckon/crew/recovery.py, called over live pointers from two projects with only one named, dispatches a review for a scoring run of the project the caller did not name. Do the reproduction in a temporary config home with the review launch stubbed, never the real fleet. Then the following hold.
(1) The help of crew recover in reckon/cli.py and the recover() docstring agree, and the help's first line names the review launch.
(2) Review dispatch from the sweep is an explicit opt-in (--dispatch-reviews). Without it, recover classifies and launches nothing. With it, recover dispatches only for the project the caller named, and an unscoped call refuses to dispatch.
(3) A review whose target's dispatching session is not live is not dispatched. It is reported as awaiting-coordinator.
(4) A review the sweep dispatches is routed to the local lane unless the reviewed node declares otherwise. Find why the measured review resolved to codex and say so in the manifest.
tests/test_recover_launches_only_what_it_is_asked.py covers each of these with the launch stubbed. The two-project case asserts that no launch occurs for the unnamed project. The cases fail at your base where the behaviour is new. Existing tests reaching recover() and crew recover keep passing; grep tests/ for recover( and crew recover to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/scoring-should-stop-a-promotion/recover-launches-only-what-it-is-asked.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
node_definition.goal: crew recover launches nothing it was not asked to, and its help says what it launches
node_definition.negative_control: With the project scope removed from the sweep's review dispatch, the two-project case in tests/test_recover_launches_only_what_it_is_asked.py records a launch for the unnamed project and fails.
